town.note: 乔阴县城: the 福林大街 runs from the 北门 (its stone arch, two stone lions; the yellow road north into the pines, which goes nowhere now, and west to 泓水南岸's foot of the hill) south past the 老姚布庄 and a three-storey tavern to the ring of flagstones round the 树王坟's raised terrace (the huge stump with its hole, the little shrine on its south side, steps down on all four sides); the 西大街 west past shops to the standing stone lion before the closed 西门 (the bookshop south of it), the 东大街 east between houses to the 东城门 and its iron lion; south the market street to the 福林楼 (east) and the 南门广场 with its great well, the willows of 翠柳湖 east of it. West along the 承安街 to the 十字路口: north the 县府衙门's gate (stone lions, the drum; its courts are a map of their own), south the rebuilt 南门 outside the city wall, then east under the 火龙将军庙 (the road runs through it below the statue's terrace) and along the lake shore back up to the square. From the square the zigzag bridge crosses the lake's lilies to the 曼雩台 and the peach grove east of it.

lion_cave.note: The dark cave under the 西大街's stone lion, the 护草神兽 in its corner: no way out but the 忘忧草's wind, or giving up (wake in the Inn).

props: the corner where two red eyes glow

east.note: East of the 东城门: the yellow-earth road (muddy in the rain) forks north on a wild winding path to the vast fog of the 云梦大泽, where travellers no longer go, and south over the 桐柏山 stone path half lost in reeds up to the 青石峪, its slopes of mottled bamboo; west down into a dense bamboo grove where a fence and a wicket gate hide the hermit's thatched hall (and its empty yard behind); south up to bare 桐柏山, scorched by the furnace in its east cliff, an old pine on a great rock.
